title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
abstract: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. Residual networks with skip connections achieve strong image classification accuracy on ImageNet.

title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
abstract: An encoder decoder convolutional network with skip connections for biomedical image segmentation trained end to end from very few images using strong data augmentation.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
abstract: Vision transformer applies a pure transformer directly to sequences of image patches and attains excellent image classification results when pre-trained on large datasets.

title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: The transformer architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions, achieves state of the art machine translation quality.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers pre-trained on unlabeled text and fine-tuned for language understanding tasks such as question answering and natural language inference.

title: Lightweight Attention Modules for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: We propose lightweight channel attention modules inserted into U-Net skip connections that improve medical image segmentation dice score while reducing parameters and inference latency.

title: Randomized Controlled Trials of Digital Interventions for Hypertension
abstract: A randomized controlled trial evaluating mobile health interventions for blood pressure control in adult patients with hypertension across primary care clinics.

title: Machine Learning for Early Sepsis Prediction in Intensive Care
abstract: Gradient boosted models trained on electronic health records predict sepsis onset in intensive care unit patients hours before clinical recognition.

title: Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research: A Survey
abstract: We survey reproducibility practices in machine learning including random seeds, variance across runs, hyperparameter reporting, code release and statistical significance testing.

title: Large Language Models as Scientific Peer Reviewers
abstract: We evaluate large language models generating peer review reports for scientific manuscripts and compare their feedback with human reviewer comments on overlap and specificity.

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Complex Reasoning
abstract: Multiple language model agents with specialized roles debate and aggregate their answers, improving factuality and reasoning compared with a single agent.

title: Focal Loss and Class Imbalance in Dense Object Detection
abstract: A focal loss down weights well classified examples, addressing extreme foreground background class imbalance in dense object detection.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: High quality image synthesis using diffusion probabilistic models trained with a weighted variational bound connected to denoising score matching.

title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Clustering with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph neural networks cluster single cell RNA sequencing gene expression profiles and identify cell types more accurately than classical approaches.

title: Statistical Pitfalls in Clinical Prediction Models
abstract: We describe common statistical pitfalls in clinical prediction modelling including overfitting, missing calibration, lack of external validation and inadequate sample size.
